About the Role:

Camunda runs on trusted data for people and agents. The Holistic Data Platform (HDP) is how we get there: a data warehouse, consumption layer, and a context layer that agents use to answer questions about pipeline, bookings, ARR and product usage. We are hiring a Data Engineer who builds that platform and also cares whether the numbers are right, whether the business uses them, and whether an agent gives a correct answer on top of them. You will work directly with Corporate Strategy, Finance, Sales, Product, and Marketing leaders.

What you'll be doing: 

 - Data Engineering:
   
   - Agent reliability. Build evals for the agents that sit on HDP. Review their answers, find the wrong ones, and fix the cause in the data, the docs, or the prompt context.
   
   - Pipelines and platform. Ingestion, orchestration, dbt, CI/CD, and cost control.

 - Machine Learning:
   
   - Help us figure out where customers are getting stuck and how we can better support them.

 - Analytics Engineering
   
   - Product Telemetry: Working with our product team to make sense of telemetry and build a better product for our customers.
   
   - Data quality as a product. Define what “correct” means for each important metric, test for it, monitor it, and tell us fast when it breaks. Reconcile HDP against data sources.
   
   - Enablement. Make it easy for analysts and business owners to get answers without you.


What you bring:

 - We’re looking for an experienced data engineer with ML/AI experience who’s comfortable working in an AI-native environment

 - Ability and/or willingness to use Camunda’s product

 - 5+ years of Data Engineering or ML experience

 - Strong data modeling skills and several years of experience with dbt.

 - Ownership mindset: we’re a small team and proud of our accomplishments

 - Experience in deploying, operating, and evolving data pipelines in the cloud (batching and streaming)

 - Knowledge of Infrastructure as code tools such as Terraform

 - Strong communication skills, enjoys sharing knowledge and learning collaboratively

 - Passion for clean code, adept at writing automated tests to maintain codebase quality and product excellence

As a Sales Engineer it’s your mission to show the value of Camunda and guide organizations planning to automate their core business processes.

You accompany prospective customers in their product evaluation of Camunda. You are responsible for achieving the product win, getting answers to all product related technical questions, and arranging all presales interactions driving the evaluation.

In this role you will partner with our Account Executives and Solution Architects, supporting you by conducting proof of concepts or handling other deeply technical discussions.  You will help qualify opportunities and then help set and execute a sales strategy to achieve a win.

The effectiveness of Camunda's Sales Engineers is gauged by their ability to convert prospects into Camunda customers both efficiently and at a high rate.

This position requires a strong interest in cutting-edge software technologies. You should take pleasure in crafting sample code or custom demonstrations and exploring new technology, even if you're not highly experienced in software development.  - Map customer requirements to our Camunda product portfolio

 - Position potential quantitative and qualitative business value of Camunda

 - Develop individual Camunda evaluation plans and demos for our prospects

 - Conduct product demos and product related Q&A sessions

 - Support the completion of RFI / RFP documents

 - Team with Account Executives to develop accounts

 - Organize and execute pre-sales engagements

 - Implement code snippets

 - Create and maintain pre-sales content and technical artifacts

 - Strong Technical Foundation:
    A degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience. Solid understanding of programming fundamentals, modern software engineering practices, and common IT/system architectures.

 - Proven Sales Engineering Experience:
    Experience in Sales Engineering or Pre-Sales, with a deep understanding of sales cycles, value-based selling, and stakeholder engagement. Skilled in handling objections and driving deals to closure in a consultative selling environment.

 - Communication Excellence:
    Exceptional presentation and interpersonal skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, compelling narratives tailored to technical and non-technical audiences alike.

 - Language Proficiency:
    Fluent in English (C-1/C-2 level or native proficiency) and one language from the region, with strong written and verbal communication

 - Travel Flexibility:
    Willingness to travel occasionally for customer meetings, events, and team collaboration.

Nice-to-haves:

 - Experience in enterprise automation, business process management (BPM), process orchestration, robotic process automation (RPA), Agentic-AI or similar domains.

 - Familiarity with value-based selling, including conducting value workshops and applying value engineering frameworks.

 - Strong understanding of the process automation and orchestration product landscape and key industry players.

 - Industry experience in BFSI, Telecommunications, or Logistics.

 - Proficiency in an additional language beyond English.

If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.



About the role:

As a Senior Software Engineer on Camunda's new Data Streaming team, you'll help build a foundational new piece of architecture that changes how customers and internal products access process data. Today, customers have no first-class way to stream their own process data out of Camunda, and Camunda's own analytics product is bottlenecked by querying the same storage the live engine depends on. You'll be part of a greenfield team rebuilding how process data is consumed and served at scale, built on top of a durable, continuously-written streaming layer that decouples data consumption from the live engine. You'll be part of a small team from day one, with real room to shape both the architecture and the team's scope as it matures.

At Camunda, we approach engineering in a holistic manner. As such, you will form strong partnerships with product management, the Data Layer and Distributed Systems teams, QA, and support, and work closely with your peers to not only deliver but directly influence how our data streaming architecture evolves to meet our customers' needs.

What You Will Do:

 - Help rebuild how Camunda's analytics product consumes and serves process data at scale, moving it off the engine's critical path entirely.

 - Design and build the core streaming infrastructure that decouples process data access from the live execution engine, backed by durable, object storage.

 - Build customer-facing data streaming capabilities, including a supported way to integrate with systems like Kafka, so customers can reliably get their process data into their own tools.

 - Make foundational architecture decisions as part of a small, high-ownership team, including how the system guarantees consistency and durability across a distributed streaming pipeline.

 - Participate in L3 support and on-call rotations, partnering with Support and SRE to investigate data layer production issues, and feeding what you learn back into the product.

What You Will Bring to the Role:

Must Haves:

 - 7+ years of experience as a backend engineer, in Java, with a strong focus on distributed or data-intensive systems.

 - Hands-on experience building or operating an analytical serving layer over a table format such as Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake - including experience with an embedded/lightweight query engine (e.g. DuckDB, or similar), or a stateful stream-processing framework (e.g. Flink, Kafka Streams).

 - A track record of working with object storage systems (S3/GCS/Azure or similar) and building reliable, idempotent upload/commit protocols against them.

 - Solid grounding in the reasoning behind correctness and consistency in data-intensive systems (e.g. concurrent writes, atomicity, idempotency).

 - A demonstrated track record of driving a technical initiative through genuine ambiguity in a still-being-designed system, not just extending an established one.

 - Proven experience leading medium-to-large engineering initiatives (3+ months) end-to-end, from solution design, project planning, and coordinating across teams, right through to driving predictable delivery.

 - Strong communication and collaboration skills in a remote-first environment: you translate requirements into actionable technical work with Product, and give and receive clear, direct feedback in code review.

Nice to Haves:

 - Experience with Kafka or a similar streaming/event-log system

 - Experience with embedded state stores (RocksDB or similar) for projection/checkpointing workloads.

 - Experience with stream processing frameworks (e.g. Apache Flink), particularly stateful processing with local state backends and checkpointing.

 - Familiarity with object-storage-native streaming architectures (e.g. systems like WarpStream) is a plus, even without direct hands-on experience.

About the role:

We're looking for a Senior Site Reliability Engineer who's passionate about building reliable, scalable infrastructure that helps developers ship better software faster. You'll design and maintain our Kubernetes-based multi-cloud platform, improve our monitoring and observability tools, and collaborate with product and engineering teams to solve real problems in real time. This is a role where you'll own the systems that power Camunda, drive automation that raises the bar for everyone, and mentor others who want to do the same. If you thrive on building things that work well and don't break when they shouldn't, we'd love to talk.

What You’ll Be Doing:

 - Design and maintain our infrastructure – You'll evolve our Kubernetes-based, multi-cloud platform architecture, ensuring it's available, scalable, and fault-tolerant. You'll establish configuration best practices and network services that our teams rely on.

 - Build observability that matters – Implement and improve monitoring and alerting tools that give both SREs and developers real visibility into system health and performance. Make it easy for teams to understand what's happening across our stack.

 - Own your systems end-to-end – You'll adopt a "you build it, you run it" mentality, which means participating in on-call rotations and being the go-to person when things need quick fixes. You'll create runbooks and automation that turn complex problems into manageable processes.

 - Ship features and improvements with product teams – Work cross-functionally with product engineering, product management, and support to define and deliver features that move the needle. Bring your expertise to the table early and often.

 - Push automation to the next level – Identify repetitive work and automate it away. Share what you learn with your teammates so everyone gets better at their craft. We measure progress by the quality of our systems, not hours worked.

 - Be the expert others learn from – Help less experienced engineers tackle complex infrastructure challenges. Break down technical problems into clear steps and support others in growing their skills. 

What You Bring:

Must Haves:

 - Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes – You've built, deployed, and maintained Kubernetes clusters in production environments. You understand how to manage workloads, networking, and storage at scale.

 - Infrastructure as code expertise – You're fluent in tools like Terraform (or similar IaC tools) and know how to version, test, and safely deploy infrastructure changes.

 - Demonstrated experience in monitoring and observability – You've worked with tools like Prometheus, Grafana, or similar platforms to instrument systems and alert on what matters.

 - Strong 3rd-level support and incident response skills – You've responded to production incidents, diagnosed complex issues, and communicated clearly with stakeholders under pressure. You understand root cause analysis and how to prevent issues from happening again.

 - A passion for automation and raising the quality bar – You see manual work as a problem to be solved. You care deeply about building systems that are reliable, maintainable, and easy to understand.

 - Responsible use of AI tools – You leverage AI for research, code review, documentation, test generation, and automation to improve your effectiveness. You know how to validate AI outputs against requirements, never share confidential or personal data with AI systems without authorization, and always retain human accountability for decisions and deliverables.

 Nice-to-haves:

 - Experience with major cloud providers – You've worked with AWS (EKS), Google Cloud Platform (GKE), or similar managed Kubernetes services.

 - ArgoCD or GitOps workflows – You've used declarative, Git-driven infrastructure management to keep systems in sync.

 - Proficiency in Python, Go, or similar languages – You write scripts and automation tools that solve real problems.

 - Experience with SLOs and alerting frameworks – You've helped teams define meaningful service level objectives and set up alerts that don't cry wolf.

About the Role: 

Hi there! We're hiring an Enterprise Account Executive III to join our Sales team.

Our sales team is tenured, technically curious, and genuinely invested in doing right by the customer, not just closing the deal in front of them. We partner closely across the business, and we operate with a lot of trust: you're given real ownership over your territory, and you're expected to bring your own judgment to how you build it.

This role carries real weight. You'll be responsible for a book of enterprise accounts where the deals are complex, the buying committees are large, and the technical bar is high. There's meaningful room here to shape how your territory gets built, not just execute against someone else's plan.

As an Enterprise Account Executive III, you'll own the full sales cycle for enterprise accounts, from first conversation through negotiation and close, working alongside sales engineering, customer success, and leadership to get complex deals across the line. This role matters because enterprise wins are how Camunda grows its footprint in large, strategic accounts, and how we prove the platform works at scale.

What You Will Do

 - Own and execute the full sales cycle for enterprise accounts, from prospecting through negotiation and close.

 - Build and drive strategic account plans that identify whitespace, map stakeholders, and set a realistic path to close.

 - Navigate complex, multi-stakeholder buying committees, including technical, business, and executive buyers.

This is a hands-on, strategic role for a rewards leader who wants to build and run programs as a trusted business partner, not just administer them. The right candidate will bring deep technical rewards expertise, strong AI and analytical skills, and a passion for a great employee experience. We also expect this leader to be AI-forward in how we approach compensation strategy and job leveling, not only in how they use AI to get their own work done. That means using AI and data-driven methods to shape pay philosophy, benchmark and model market data, design and calibrate our job architecture and leveling framework, and make faster, more consistent, and more transparent rewards decisions.

What you'll be doing:

 -  Own the global Total Rewards strategy across compensation, benefits, equity, and recognition, and make sure it helps Camunda attract, retain, and motivate top talent. Set an AI-forward vision for how Camunda designs and runs compensation, and turn it into a practical roadmap.

 - Lead the annual compensation cycle, including merit, promotion, and equity planning, in partnership with People Business Partners, Finance, and business leaders.

 - Own job architecture, leveling, and grading frameworks, and keep the Job Catalog accurate as the company grows. Apply AI and data-driven approaches to job leveling, such as consistent role-to-level mapping, calibration, and level-drift detection, with human oversight.

 - Run market benchmarking and compensation analysis, and turn the findings into clear, data-driven recommendations for leadership. Use AI to speed up and improve benchmarking, pay modeling, and scenario analysis.

 - Manage benefits programs and vendor relationships across regions, including EOR providers such as Remote.com http://Remote.com, brokers, and equity administration platforms, with a clear view of cost, service levels, and employee value.

 - Ensure compliance with pay transparency, pay equity, and local compensation and benefits regulations in every jurisdiction where Camunda operates.

 - Partner with Finance on compensation budgeting and equity pool management, and track total rewards spend against a clear baseline.

 - Advise People Business Partners and hiring managers on offers, pay decisions, and exceptions, balancing internal equity, market data, budget and capturing and retaining strong AI talent..

 - Identify and adopt AI and automation tools that improve rewards analytics, benchmarking, and employee communications, and ensure AI use complies with local laws and regulations.

 - Lead, coach, and develop the Total Rewards team, setting clear priorities and growth paths.

 - Manage Camunda’s Relationship with our EOR.

 - 8+ years of Total Rewards experience, including significant compensation and benefits experience at a global, multi-country technology or SaaS company.

 - Hands-on experience leading a global compensation cycle (merit, promotion, and equity) and running market benchmarking with tools such as Radford, Pave, or similar.

 - Experience managing benefits, EOR, and equity vendor relationships, including platforms such as Remote or similar.

 - Strong analytical and modeling skills, with the ability to translate complex data into practical, business-pragmatic recommendations.

 - Working knowledge of pay transparency, pay equity, and compensation regulations across multiple jurisdictions, ideally including the EU and USA.

 - Experience using AI and automation tools to improve rewards analytics and workflows.

 - AI-forward approach to compensation strategy and job leveling, with real examples of using AI or advanced analytics to shape pay philosophy, model market data, build or calibrate job architecture and levels, or improve pay decisions, and the judgment to keep humans accountable for fairness, compliance, and explainability.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to build trust across People, Finance, and Legal.

 - Experience leading or developing a team and influencing senior stakeholders.

 - Own positioning and messaging for your product area, translating technical capability into a clear value proposition for both technical and business buyers.

 - Build and maintain a competitive intelligence program that sales actually uses, not just battlecards that sit in a folder.

 - Lead go-to-market execution for launches in your area, coordinating across product, sales, and demand gen so the message is consistent everywhere it shows up.

 - Arm the field with content that works in real conversations: pitch decks, demos, solution briefs, and objection handling.

 - Use market and customer research to inform product and positioning decisions, not just to validate ones already made.

 - Mentor and support other marketers on your team, sharing what you've learned without being asked.

 - Comfort marketing technical products to technical buyers. You can go deep enough into a technical concept to be credible with a developer, and simplify it enough to be clear to an executive.

About the role:

ProcessOS is a new kind of Camunda product: business processes described in natural language, generated as executable BPMN workflows, and improved autonomously from production data. We’re hiring the first cohort of Forward Deployed Engineers to bring it into production at enterprise customers. You’ll own the deployment journey from first process file to a working, improving system, and hand off a functioning capability to the customer’s team. The code you write and the patterns you discover feed directly back into how ProcessOS is built. This is a rare opportunity to shape a product, a function, and a field practice from day one.

You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.


What You’ll Be Doing:

 -  Deploy and prove. Own the journey from first process file to production workflow. At 90 days: at least one workflow running, the improvement loop active, and measurable fitness gains the customer can see. At 12 months: 3–5 customers with viable deployments.

 - Drive organizational adoption. Work across technical and business stakeholders to build understanding and trust, turning early deployments into lasting customer capability.

 - Work at depth technically. Configure and run Camunda clusters locally and in cloud environments. Debug integration failures. Build custom agents where platform defaults don’t fit. Write connector logic that gets legacy enterprise systems talking to ProcessOS.

 - Build the playbook. There is no deployment template yet. Document what good looks like as you discover it, and make the next implementation faster.

 - Feed the product. Custom agents you write get contributed back. Integration patterns get codified. Production bugs you find, you often fix. Your field work is a direct input to ProcessOS.

 - Hand off deliberately. Leave customers with a team that can operate independently, is trained on the platform, and acts on improvement results without you.



What You Will Bring to the Role

Must Haves:

 - Enterprise production experience: you’ve shipped something inside a large organization and stayed to see it operate. You know why governance and resilience matter at scale.

 - Technical depth: You can debug an integration failure, write a custom agent against a legacy API, stand up a Camunda cluster from scratch, and explain generated BPMN to both engineers and business leads.

 - Stakeholder communication: you work effectively across engineering, architecture, and business leadership and adapt how you communicate without losing precision.

 - Practical AI experience: you’ve used AI to solve real problems in production – not just experimented. You understand context management, prompt engineering, agent testing, and integration tradeoffs.

 - Comfort with ambiguity: you make sound judgment calls without a playbook and document what you learn.

 - Occasional travel may be required

Nice to Haves:

 - Experience in a customer-facing engineering or professional services role.

 - Familiarity with regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or insurance

 - Production experience with agentic systems or AI-integrated workflows.

 - Contributions to a shared platform or open source project that others built on.

About the role:

Hi there! We're seeking a strategic and operationally excellent Senior Compensation Operations Manager to own the design, implementation, and governance of our enterprise sales compensation program. This senior-level individual contributor role reports to the VP of Revenue Operations and serves as the architect and steward of compensation strategy across our diverse go-to-market organization.

You'll partner with GTM Leadership, Finance, and People Operations to build world-class compensation programs that attract talent, drive the right behaviors, and align with business objectives. You'll manage the full lifecycle of compensation—from design through implementation, compliance, analytics, and continuous improvement—across Account Executives, Sales Engineers, Sales Leaders, Partner Managers, Customer Success Managers, Technical Account Managers and other functions on variable compensation plans.

Note: This role focuses on compensation design and operations. Our Finance team manages commission accounting and invoice processing in Xactly.



What You Will Do


COMPENSATION STRATEGY & DESIGN

 - Own the strategic design of annual sales compensation programs for all eligible roles and adjust for market conditions, competitive landscape, and business priorities

 - Benchmark compensation against market data and peer software companies; conduct pay equity analysis and recommend adjustments to ensure competitiveness and fairness

 - Design commission structures, accelerators, quotas, and incentive mechanics that drive desired sales behaviors and align with revenue goals

 - Design and own SPIFF and other incentive programs outside of the official incentive plan

 - Lead cross-functional design reviews with Sales, Finance, and executive leadership to validate programs before launch


PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION & OPERATIONS

 - Manage the end-to-end program launch calendar; coordinate cross-functional efforts and communicate timelines, changes, and deadlines to stakeholders

 - Build and maintain the primary source of truth for all compensation program documentation, including plan documents, commission schedules, quota assignments, and policy guidelines

 - Configure compensation programs in Xactly and SFDC; validate data integrity, test calculations, and ensure system configurations reflect approved plan design

 - Develop training materials and lead training sessions for sales teams on compensation plan mechanics, commission calculations, and incentive rules


GOVERNANCE & COMPLIANCE

 - Ensure compensation programs comply with applicable laws, regulations, and company policies across all geographies where we operate

 - Manage exceptions, disputes, and appeals related to commissions, quotas, and incentive payouts; work with VP RevOps, Finance and HR to resolve efficiently and fairly

 - Maintain audit trails and documentation for all material compensation decisions and changes


ANALYTICS & REPORTING

 - Build dashboards and reports to monitor role based performance metrics, compensation spend, payout distributions, plan attainment, and ROI on incentive investments.  Including SPIFF reporting metrics

 - Conduct post-program analysis (win/loss, attainment distribution, program metrics) and deliver insights to leadership on plan effectiveness

 - Recommend program adjustments mid-year based on market shifts, business performance, and feedback from sales leaders


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Partner with VP of RevOps to align compensation with business strategy and sales priorities; maintain regular feedback loops with Sales Leaders

 - Work directly with Commission Accounting on attainment data, payouts, calculations and discrepancies

 - Collaborate with Finance on budgeting, forecasting, and year-end reporting of incentive spend

 - Work with People Operations on equity, total rewards strategy, and talent retention initiatives

 - Communicate compensation strategy and changes to the broader organization with clarity and confidence



What You Will Bring to the Role


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - 8+ years of progressive experience in sales compensation, incentive design, or related revenue operations roles (within software, SaaS, or enterprise sales environments preferred)

 - Demonstrated expertise in designing and managing compensation programs for multiple sales roles and structures

 - Advanced proficiency with sales compensation platforms (Xactly, Anaplan, SAP SuccessFactors, or equivalent); strong data analysis and Excel skills

 - Deep understanding of CRM systems (Salesforce preferred) and comfort configuring objects, fields, and reporting for incentive programs

 - Strong project management and cross-functional collaboration skills; ability to influence without authority and manage competing priorities

 - Excellent communication and presentation skills; comfort translating complex compensation concepts for diverse audiences (sales teams, executives, finance, HR)

 - Meticulous attention to detail; strong analytical and problem-solving abilities

 - Familiarity with GDPR, CCPA, and other employment law considerations affecting compensation (particularly for global organizations)


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience managing compensation programs across multiple geographic regions with different regulatory requirements

 - Background in financial analysis, FP&A, or accounting; understanding of revenue recognition impacts on compensation timing

 - Exposure to Customer Success, Services, or other non-traditional sales comp models

 - Certification in compensation (e.g., WorldatWork CECP, GRP) or related HR disciplines

 - Experience at a high-growth or publicly traded software company

We are looking for an Enterprise Account Executive to build Camunda’s Dutch Government market. This is a territory-building role for a disciplined, consultative seller who can create demand, shape strategic opportunities, and guide complex buying groups through to executive-level decisions. You will own the full sales cycle across a focused set of government accounts, from account strategy and first conversation through business case, procurement, negotiation, close, and expansion.

You will combine commercial ownership with public-sector credibility. The successful candidate will be comfortable engaging senior civil servants, CIO and transformation leaders, procurement, security, architecture, and business stakeholders. You will translate government priorities into a compelling value case for process orchestration, automation, and agentic workflows, while navigating formal procurement processes and the governance expectations of public-sector customers.




WHAT YOU WILL OWN

 - Own the Dutch Government territory and create a clear account and coverage strategy across priority national and public-sector organizations.

 - Build and maintain a healthy, self-generated pipeline, targeting at least 2.5x pipeline coverage through focused outbound activity, executive engagement, partner collaboration, and market development.

 - Develop relationships across complex buying groups, including CIOs, CTOs, transformation leaders, enterprise architects, process owners, procurement, security, legal, and executive sponsors.

 - Lead the full enterprise sales cycle: discovery, qualification, value engineering, technical evaluation, business case, procurement, commercial negotiation, and close.

 - Apply MEDDICC consistently to create deal clarity, strengthen qualification, identify gaps early, and improve forecast reliability.

 - Build business cases connected to public-sector outcomes such as service quality, operational efficiency, transparency, resilience, compliance, and cost control.

 - Coordinate account teams across Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Professional Services, Marketing, Product, Legal, Finance, and leadership.

 - Developa partner-first motion with relevant global system integrators, regional partners, and public-sector specialists.

 - Expand successful customer relationships by identifying adjacent processes, departments, agencies, and use cases after the initial land.

 - Maintain accurate account, contact, opportunity, and forecast data in Salesforce as the single source of truth.

 - Share market intelligence on government priorities, procurement dynamics, competitors, partners, and customer needs to improve Camunda’s Dutch public-sector go-to-market strategy.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

First 30 days

 - Build a working understanding of Camunda’s platform, value proposition, sales methodology, customer evidence, pricing approach, and public-sector references.

 - Align with internal stakeholders on territory priorities, account ownership, partner coverage, and available sales resources.

 - Produce an initial account segmentation and stakeholder-mapping plan for the Dutch Government territory.

 - Establish a repeatable operating cadence for pipeline creation, deal inspection, forecasting, and cross-functional account-team collaboration.

First 90 days

 - Complete strategic account plans for the highest-priority government accounts, including business priorities, buying groups, whitespace, partners, competition, and next actions.

 - Create qualified pipeline through a balanced mix of net-new opportunities, partner-sourced activity, executive introductions, and expansion plays.

 - Develop a strong network of relevant government and ecosystem stakeholders, with clear relationship and meeting objectives.

 - Demonstrate consistent MEDDICC qualification and accurate Salesforce hygiene across active opportunities.

 - Identify the most relevant public-sector use cases and value narratives for Camunda’s Dutch market development.

First 180 days and beyond

 - Establish a credible, repeatable pipeline engine for the Dutch Government market.

 - Progress strategic opportunities through well-defined qualification, value validation, technical evaluation, procurement, and commercial stages.

 - Win new government logos and create expansion paths into additional departments, agencies, or processes.

 - Build trusted relationships with executive sponsors and public-sector ecosystem partners.

 - Contribute actionable market insight that improves Camunda’s positioning, messaging, partner strategy, and investment decisions in the Netherlands.

 - Deliver against quota while protecting long-term customer value, adoption, and expansion potential.


WHAT YOU WILL BRING

Must-haves

 - 5+ years of success in a quota-carrying enterprise software or SaaS Account Executive role, owning complex deals end to end.

 - Demonstrated experience selling into the Dutch Government or another highly regulated public-sector environment, with a clear understanding of formal procurement, security, legal, and governance requirements.

 - A track record of creating pipeline through proactive outbound activity and converting multi-stakeholder opportunities into material, preferably multi-year, contracts.

 - Strong command of MEDDICC or a comparable enterprise sales methodology, with the discipline to qualify rigorously, manage mutual action plans, and forecast accurately.

 - Executive presence and communication skills in Dutch and English, with the ability to connect operational problems to strategic, financial, and citizen-impact outcomes.

 - A collaborative, customer-focused, and resilient approach aligned with Camunda’s FAITH values and global-first way of working.

Nice-to-haves

 - Experience selling process automation, workflow, orchestration, integration, business transformation, or adjacent enterprise technology.

 - Existing relationships across Dutch ministries, executive agencies, municipalities, provinces, public-service organizations, or government-focused partners.

 - Experience working with global system integrators, regional implementation partners, or public-sector framework agreements.

 - Familiarity with Camunda, BPMN, DMN, process orchestration, cloud platforms, or agentic automation.

 - Experience creating quantified value cases for service modernization, compliance, operational resilience, or cost reduction.


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS NOW

Dutch public-sector organizations are under pressure to modernize services, improve efficiency, operate securely, and coordinate increasingly complex technology and regulatory environments. Process orchestration gives them a way to make that complexity visible and manageable while connecting people, systems, and automation.

This role is an opportunity to shape a market rather than inherit a mature patch. You will have the ownership and visibility to define where Camunda can create the greatest public value, build the ecosystem around those opportunities, and establish a durable foundation for growth in the Netherlands.

You will join a global, distributed team that values initiative, transparency, customer impact, and practical collaboration. The role offers the chance to work at the intersection of public-sector transformation, enterprise technology, process orchestration, and the next generation of agentic automation.

About the Role:

Mission

Own the experience of everything customers and agents use without a UI: the public API, CLI, SDKs, and configuration. Make it fast to get to production and trustworthy once there, and make it the interface of the future for agents.


TIME SPLIT

30% Strategy

 - Own the overall headless experience across products, making it the interface agents prefer to work with, held to a consistently high design bar

 - Define and evolve API and developer-experience conventions (patterns, consistency, error handling, documentation standards)

 - Treat agent-facing surfaces (MCP servers, tool descriptions, schemas, CLI output) as designed products, not by-products of the API

 - Define how we measure agent experience (agent task success rate, error recovery rate, tool-call efficiency) and test designs with agents as well as with people

 - Set the standard for how agents discover, call, and recover from errors in our APIs and tools

 - Collaborate with Product, FDE, Marketing, and Legal on topics that touch the headless experience

 - Align with the UI/UX product designer so UI and headless feel like one product (shared terminology, patterns, journeys)

 - Enable builders with tools, training, and guidance, and give feedback on epics

70% Initiative work

 - Co-own assigned initiatives with the PM

 - Own the headless customer journey and experience of each initiative, from first API call to production operation

 - Focus on Time to First Production and Production Confidence

 - Design the agent journey inside each initiative: how an agent builds, runs, and operates the solution on a user's behalf, including recovery when a call fails


LEVEL

Senior. The role combines hands-on initiative work with shaping principles that outlast any single initiative. If the scope grows toward setting direction across teams, we will revisit Principal.



What You Will Do

 - Own the headless experience as one product with clear ownership and a real design bar

 - Shorten the path from first API call to running in production

 - Build confidence that teams can trust the API in operation

 - Design for agents as first-class users, alongside humans

 - Keep one experience together with the UI/UX product designer at the seam between UI and headless

 - Enable builders so API design quality does not depend on one person

About the Role:

Camunda Hub is where enterprises run Camunda at scale. From Hub they manage their clusters and tenants, decide who can do what, and roll changes out across the whole organization. We’re looking for a Senior Product Builder to own the backend and architecture that let Hub manage a whole fleet of clusters. Your first focus will be the mechanism that sends access, secret, tenant and licence changes out to every connected cluster and brings deployments, health and audit records back. From there, you’ll shape Hub’s foundations: its event model, the service boundaries and data model other teams build on, and how Hub behaves when things fail or get upgraded. The platform is your product. Your users are platform administrators, Centres of Excellence and the builders across Camunda who depend on what you create. You’ll join a new two-person pod in our remote-first team. You’ll have real ownership as the person who makes the call, and you’ll build AI-first, from written specs through to production. Our customers run mission-critical processes on Camunda, so your work will matter to them every day.

What You Will Do:

 - Take over Hub's fleet propagation mechanism from the team building its first version, and make it work for access, secrets, tenants, licences and custom roles

 - Write short design documents for foundational changes, get them reviewed by the teams that depend on them, and turn them into tested, shipped code

 - Design how Hub behaves when things go wrong: offline clusters, partial failures, Hub outages, and clusters being adopted or detached

 - Build the path from clusters back to Hub, starting with deployment inventory, health, audit records and licence status

 - Design Hub's first event and webhook mechanism, so admins and agents can react to changes instead of polling for them

 - Join the pod's rotations and Hub on-call, and help other builders take on backend work through reviews, guidelines and contract tests

What You Will Bring to the Role:

 - Experience building and running backend systems in production that other teams or customers depend on

 - Comfort taking a problem nobody owns yet and turning it into a design, a plan and shipped code

 - Product judgment for technical users: you talk to the people who use your APIs and make trade-offs on their behalf

 - Clear, short writing that lets a remote team review and decide asynchronously

 - Care for how a system behaves when parts of it fail, not only for the happy path

Must Haves:

 - Designed and shipped a control plane or similar system that pushes desired state to many targets. Knows outbox or event-log patterns, idempotent apply, versioning, retries and drift reconciliation

 - Senior backend engineering in Java (API design, relational data models, multi-tenant SaaS services) and hands-on Helm and Kubernetes for self-managed installations

 - Software architecture and failure analysis: partial failure, blast radius, consistency trade-offs. Has debugged production incidents in a distributed system and is ready for on-call

 - Has shaped an API or platform as a product, and writes design docs other teams can build on. Gets agreement across teams without formal authority

 - Builds AI-first from written specifications and checks AI output as carefully as any other code

Nice to Haves:

 - Kubernetes operators or GitOps tools, for example Argo CD

 - OIDC, SCIM and permission models, or secret managers and licence systems

 - Camunda 8 or another workflow or orchestration engine

 - Enough frontend skill to build a thin UI on top of a backend capability

About the Role:

Partners are a core growth engine at Camunda.

As a Senior Partner Director you are the field execution arm of our partner strategy in Iberia and LATAM. You will work with the global and regional system integrators, specialist firms and technology partners who bring Camunda into customer accounts, and you will work side by side with our sales teams to turn those relationships into qualified pipeline, certified practitioners and closed business.

You will not be managing relationships for their own sake. You will own the regional plan, the named target accounts and the next actions for partners in your territory, and you will be measured on the pipeline and revenue they help create.

Strategy and ownership are clear by design. Global partner leads own the strategy, relationship and contract decisions for our strategic global system integrators. You own regional execution and the CRM record for partner opportunities. Account Executives own the customer opportunity, forecast, pricing and close plan. You will work across all three and escalate early when they pull in different directions.

What you'll be doing:

 -  Regional plan: build and run the regional partner plan for your territory, translating our global partner strategy into named accounts, partner plays and clear owners. Write a one-page regional execution plan for each priority global system integrator and give input on partner tiering and resourcing.

 - Target accounts and joint planning: partner with Account Executives and regional sales leaders to map target accounts, run account mapping sessions with partners and build joint account plans. Agree one specific ask of the partner for each target account, and join discovery calls, workshops, demos and executive meetings.

 - Pipeline and deal execution: qualify and advance partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities. Run a weekly pipeline review with Sales, form small cross-functional pursuit teams for material opportunities, and keep next steps, deal registration and attribution accurate in our CRM.

 - Partner activation and enablement: activate and enable partners locally with a 30-60-90 day activation plan for each new partner, covering onboarding, sales readiness, certification and awareness sessions. Help partners build named Camunda practices with certified consultants, and work with Sales Engineering on technical support for pursuits.

 - Events and joint marketing: plan and run partner events, executive field activity and joint marketing with our Marketing teams, tied to target accounts and pipeline.

 - Global alignment and escalation: work with our global partner leads so that regional execution supports global relationships. Support local country agreements with the global owner, and escalate channel conflicts, exclusivity requests, disputed attribution and commercial questions early, following the agreed escalation path.

 - Commercial discipline: make sure no partner commitment is made without written approval, and contribute inputs to business cases for partner investment. Pricing, discounts, legal terms and the customer forecast are owned by others, and you will bring them in when needed.

 - Forecast, reporting and cadence: provide weekly pipeline and forecast inputs and risk reporting, contribute to the regional partner review, monthly status and a quarterly partner scorecard, and keep action, decision and risk logs current with named owners and dates.

Additional responsibilities at Senior level

The Senior Partner Director takes on regional leadership on top of regional execution. In addition to the above, you will:

 - Cover a multi-country geography or a top segment with several sales teams, and set the territory plan with limited steer

 - Own the business plan for the territory and the quality of execution plans and joint account plans across it

 - Co-lead plays with global system integrators and act as the named regional counterpart for priority partners

 - Engage partner regional and global alliance leaders and Camunda regional sales leadership, and join partner executive reviews

 - Lead the move from champion-led relationships to practice-led relationships, where a certified practice sells and delivers Camunda

 - Draft business cases for partner investment and market development funds, for approval by leadership and Finance

 - Co-present the quarterly business review with the Regional Partner Leader

 - Coach peers, act as onboarding buddy for new joiners, share playbooks, and lead regional or cross-region working groups

 - Resolve routine cross-region coordination directly and escalate only true conflicts

What you bring:

 - Ability and/or willingness to use our product https://accounts.cloud.camunda.io/signup?_ga=2.47330343.127558761.1654184528-504024057.1654184528.

 - Experience building partner revenue in enterprise software, ideally with system integrators and regional implementation partners (typically 8 or more years for Regional Partner Director and 12 or more for Senior)

 - A track record of working inside a direct sales motion and creating pipeline with partners, not only managing the relationship

 - Strong commercial understanding of partner models such as resale, referral, co-sell, deal registration and attribution

 - Confidence engaging senior leaders at partners and customers, and the ability to build a joint business plan and hold partners to it

 - Operational discipline with CRM, forecasting and action tracking, including clean pipeline hygiene and accurate attribution

 - Comfort working in a matrix, where strategy, regional execution and the customer deal have different owners

 - Fluent in English and Spanish

 - Willingness to travel within your region for partner meetings and events

 - Senior level: experience coaching peers or leading cross-functional or cross-region initiatives, and engaging partner executives at regional and global level

Nice to haves

 - Knowledge of process orchestration, workflow automation, BPM or AI agent platforms

 - Experience building certified practices inside system integrators

 - Experience with cloud marketplace and hyperscaler co-sell motions

How we measure success

We look at outcomes, health and capability rather than activity counts. Your scorecard will cover:

 - Outcomes: qualified partner pipeline created or influenced, closed-won revenue contribution with sourced and influenced reported separately, and completion of target-account plans

 - Health: next-action hygiene, forecast accuracy, CRM completeness and deal registration turnaround

 - Capability and speed: partner activation, certified practitioners and time to first opportunity

 - Senior level: pipeline coverage across the portfolio, forecast accuracy and the development of peers

What success looks like

 - First 30 days: you meet your partners, sales counterparts and the global partner owners, confirm ownership, baseline the pipeline in your territory and agree a first target-account set.

 - By 60 days: you run a regular execution rhythm with sales and partners, including the regular regional review and pursuit teams for material opportunities, with named customer actions and partner actions and visible movement on opportunities.

 - By 90 days: you have a regional plan linked to the global plan, a first partner scorecard and a clear view of which partnerships to scale, repair or pause. Any investment asks are presented as proposals, not assumed approvals.

About the Role:

We run Camunda on Camunda. Our Enterprise Agentic Automation Team (EAAT) builds production-grade agentic orchestration on Camunda’s platform for Camunda’s own operations, from Finance to Support to Go-to-Market.

As Senior Architect, you lead our most complex EAAT-led initiative from discovery to production. You partner with process owners to find where the value is, redesign how the work should flow in an AI-first company, decide where agents, rules or people handle each step, and shape it into scope our engineers build from directly. Then you lead delivery with the engineers until it’s live and the value is proven.

This is a delivery role with architecture depth: you design within our reference architecture, prototype to de-risk, and lead the engineers who build it. You stay until it works in production, and keep evolving it.

What You Will Do:

 - Own delivery of our use cases end to end, business and technical, from discovery to production and value realization

 - Redesign processes for agentic AI with process owners: start from an as-is baseline and design the orchestration (where agents, rules or humans handle each step), the engagement layer (how people interact with the process and its agents) and the context agents need to do it well

 - Turn target processes into epics engineers can build from directly: scenarios, acceptance criteria, increments

 - Design solutions within our reference architecture, and bring new patterns based on lessons learned

 - Lead technical delivery on your initiatives: plan increments with the engineers, manage dependencies and risks, and keep process owners and sponsors aligned on progress and decisions

 - Define and track value per initiative and increment, and keep business decisions moving

This is a strong entry point into tech sales for someone who wants to learn and refine the fundamentals of prospecting, discovery, and pipeline generation inside an enterprise software motion. You'll work directly with Account Executives but will also be responsible for prospecting into your own patch. We ask that all of our ADRs have a remote environment that is conducive to consistent weekly motions and to be able to travel 4-6 times per year, usually a week or less at a time.

As an ADR I, you'll run long-term outbound and timely inbound prospecting motions to generate qualified pipeline for our sales team. Working emails, sales cadences, social outreach and most importantly calls to get in front of the right people at the right accounts at the right time. This role exists because a sustainable pipeline is built through persistence, consistency, a growth mindset and an ability to diagnose challenges and bring solutions within your own prospecting motion.

What you'll be doing:

 -  Generate qualified pipeline by running outbound prospecting across email, phone, event outreach and attendance and LinkedIn into target accounts.

 - Qualify inbound interest through ADR-led scheduled calls and convert into booked meetings for Account Executives.

 - Research accounts, personas and signals to tailor and leverage AI for high touch low impact motions.

 - Partner with Account Executives to understand what constitutes a quality meeting, contact and account, and adjust your approach based on feedback.

 - Exhibit excellent operational hygiene by tracking activity and pipeline health in Salesforce and other sales tools to monitor your own inputs and performance.

 - Learn Camunda's product and value propositions and the process orchestration space well enough to have credible, useful conversations with prospects in specific verticals.

 - Some experience with outbound prospecting or customer-facing communication is preferred. This doesn't have to be in sales. Internships, retail, hospitality, or customer support all count if you know how to build rapport with people, manage expectations and handle rejection.

 - Comfort with strict time management and prioritization of requests. You'll be conducting a lot of calls and emails, and you're motivated by the math of it. You will also be given regular enablement and will be responsible for monitoring multiple sources of leads.

 - Curiosity about technology and a willingness to learn a technical product. You don't need an engineering background, but you need to be genuinely interested in understanding what Camunda does and why it matters to the people you're calling. You share successes.

 - Resilience and self-awareness. You know how to keep going without getting discouraged, and you can tell the difference between a bad day and a bad approach.

 - Coachability. You take feedback from your manager and AEs seriously and change your approach in a timely and meaningful way based on it.

About the role:

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk https://www.camundacon.com/event-session/camundacon-amsterdam-2025/one-exporter-to-rule-them-all-exploring-camunda-exporter/?on_demand=true from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale



What You’ll Be Doing:

We are looking for a Product Builder to join the IDP & RPA pod. You will take real problems from customers, decide what is worth solving, and build and ship the solution yourself, using AI tools to get from idea to production quickly without lowering the bar.



Product Building is how Camunda's Experience organization builds the applications people use on top of Camunda 8, such as Hub, Operate, and ProcessOS. Small pods of builders own a product area from customer problem to shipped change, with no hand-offs between product management, design, and engineering. We are setting this model up now, so you will help shape how it works.



The IDP & RPA pod builds how Camunda processes work with documents and legacy applications. With intelligent document processing (IDP), customers create extraction and classification templates in Camunda Hub and publish them so a process can use AI to turn invoices and other documents into structured data. With robotic process automation (RPA), customers integrate legacy applications that have no APIs, using Robot Framework scripts on a standalone RPA worker. The hard problems come with putting LLMs into customer processes: extraction quality, model and prompt choices, testing and trust, and working for AI agents as well as for people.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Help shape product direction for IDP & RPA by combining customer input, usage data, and field feedback into clear priorities.

 - Partner with the other builders and product strategy to turn problems into shipped features, using short written proposals and prototypes to align early.

 - Make judgment calls with incomplete information within your scope and own the outcome.

 - Communicate trade-offs and decisions clearly to stakeholders who don't live in the details the way you do.

 - Use AI tools across the whole loop, from specs to prototypes to production-ready code, and hold a high bar for what you ship by reviewing and improving the output rather than accepting it.

 - Build, test, and ship improvements to the IDP & RPA experience, reading errors and tracing issues far enough to give your pod useful context.

 - Talk to customers and to support and customer success colleagues about how IDP is used and where it breaks, and turn what you learn into decisions about what to build next.

 - Pick up customer incidents and trace them across Hub, the connectors, and the deployed process of the customer.

 - Track what you ship against real outcomes and adjust when the data tells you to.

 - Ability and/or willingness to use our product https://accounts.cloud.camunda.io/signup?_ga=2.47330343.127558761.1654184528-504024057.1654184528

If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.



About the Role:

Hi there! We're hiring an Information Security Engineer with a focus on Application Security to join our Information Security team at Camunda.



We are a team that takes security seriously without making it feel like a locked door. We work in a transparent, straightforward way, and we care about doing the work right rather than just checking a compliance box.



You will work side by side with our R&D engineers: reviewing designs, threat modeling new features, digging into code and helping teams make good, risk-based decisions about the vulnerabilities that come in. You'll also help build the internal tools that make this work scale, including our CVE registry and the LLM-assisted workflows we use to analyse code and triage findings.

Camunda is an AI-first company, and InfoSec is no exception: AI agents are part of how we review code, assess vulnerabilities, and build our tools. You will help shape how that works.



This is a hands-on role for someone who already has solid AppSec foundations and wants to grow. We are a generalist team, so you will also take part in our on-call rotation and incident response, and get exposure to other areas of security. But most of your time will be spent with engineers and building and maintaining internal tools and processes.



What You Will Do

 - Vulnerability management: triage findings from SCA, container and code scanning, external reports and internal security testing; assess whether Camunda is actually affected; agree fix / mitigate / accept with engineering and follow through to release.

 - Threat modeling and security reviews: run threat modeling sessions and design reviews with R&D teams for new features and architecture changes, and turn the results into concrete, prioritised actions.

 - Code analysis with LLMs: use and improve LLM-assisted tooling (agents, prompts, reusable skills) to review code, validate findings and reproduce issues, while applying your own judgement to know when the model is wrong.

 - Build internal security tooling: contribute to the CVE registry and related automation that connects scanners, engineering teams, and customer communication. Much of it is built on Camunda itself.

 - Help engineers do the secure thing by default: answer questions, review pull requests, improve guidelines and occasionally run a session or workshop.

 - On-call and incident response: share the InfoSec on-call rotation with the other engineers and help investigate and resolve security incidents.

 - Support the wider team: help write security advisories for our customers, answer customer security questions and support audits.

What You Will Bring to the Role

 - Around 3+ years in security or software engineering, with at least 2 of them working on application or product security (AppSec, product security, pentesting, or a security-focused developer role all count).

 - Experience at a SaaS or software product company, working closely with engineering teams that ship often through modern CI/CD and cloud environments.

 - Hands-on vulnerability triage: you've worked with tools like Snyk, Trivy, Semgrep, CodeQL or similar, can tell a real issue from a false positive, and can explain how exploitable something actually is in context (CVSS, exploitability,  configuration).

 - Threat modeling and design review experience (e.g. STRIDE) on real systems, ideally web apps, APIs, or distributed services.

 - You read and write code. You're comfortable reading Java (Camunda is built on it) well enough to follow a data flow and spot a security bug. You can write scripts and small tools and contribute to an existing codebase with review.

 - You build with AI, not just chat with it. You use AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar) in your daily work to write tools, analyse code or automate tasks. And you know their output still needs a second look, especially when it comes to security.

 - Clear, friendly communication with engineers. You see yourself as an enabler, not a gatekeeper, and you can explain risk to people who aren't security specialists.



Nice to haves

 - Some Python and/or JavaScript experience, or experience building internal tools.

 - Willingness to learn and use Camunda, since we build a lot of our own security automation on it. Prior BPMN / workflow experience is a plus.

 - Experience responding to security incidents or being part of an on-call rotation.

 - Exposure to security advisories, CVE disclosure or bug bounty programmes.

 - Knowledge of AI/LLM security risks (OWASP Top 10 for LLMs / agentic apps, prompt injection, tool abuse).

 - Experience securing Kubernetes or container-based workloads, or open-source / B2B software.

About the Role:

As an AI Forward Deployed ProcessOS is a new kind of Camunda product: business processes described in natural language, generated as executable BPMN workflows, and improved autonomously from production data. We’re hiring the first cohort of Forward Deployed Engineers to bring it into production at enterprise customers. You’ll own the deployment journey from first process file to a working, improving system, and hand off a functioning capability to the customer’s team. The code you write and the patterns you discover feed directly back into how ProcessOS is built. This is a rare opportunity to shape a product, a function, and a field practice from day one.


You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.

What you'll be doing:

 -  Deploy and prove. Own the journey from first process file to production workflow. At 90 days: at least one workflow running, the improvement loop active, and measurable fitness gains the customer can see. At 12 months: 3–5 customers with viable deployments.

 - Drive organizational adoption. Work across technical and business stakeholders to build understanding and trust, turning early deployments into lasting customer capability.

 - Work at depth technically. Configure and run Camunda clusters locally and in cloud environments. Debug integration failures. Build custom agents where platform defaults don’t fit. Write connector logic that gets legacy enterprise systems talking to ProcessOS.

 - Build the playbook. There is no deployment template yet. Document what good looks like as you discover it, and make the next implementation faster.

 - Feed the product. Custom integrations you write get contributed back. Integration patterns get codified. Production bugs you find, you often fix. Your field work is a direct input to ProcessOS.

 - Hand off deliberately. Leave customers with a team that can operate independently, is trained on the platform, and acts on improvement results without you.

What you bring:

 - Ability and/or willingness to use our product https://accounts.cloud.camunda.io/signup?_ga=2.47330343.127558761.1654184528-504024057.1654184528.

 - Enterprise production experience: you’ve shipped something inside a large organization and stayed to see it operate. You know why governance and resilience matter at scale.

 - Technical depth: You can debug an integration failure, write a custom agent against a legacy API, stand up a Camunda cluster from scratch, and explain generated BPMN to both engineers and business leads.

 - Stakeholder communication: you work effectively across engineering, architecture, and business leadership and adapt how you communicate without losing precision.

 - Practical AI experience: you’ve used AI to solve real problems in production – not just experimented. You understand context management, prompt engineering, agent testing, and integration tradeoffs.

 - Comfort with ambiguity: you make sound judgment calls without a playbook and document what you learn.

 - Occasional travel may be required

 - Familiarity with regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or insurance
